title: A kb/_self doc worker's brief has it run the landing's own eval, or compare with its pre-edit noted count
goal: The brief rule bl_dispatch.self_eval_rules gives a worker whose touches name a kb/_self doc either the eval command land runs (backlog.json land_eval, all roots, whose noted= is compared with NOTED_BASELINE) or a comparison of the _self noted= count with the count before its edits, so a reword that adds notes and stops land's eval step fails the worker's own run. Found by the SP-kbrxa4c4 review (S2, ST-sgzhsq4p): the _self-only noted is 4 against a baseline of 13, while the all-root noted already equals 13.

run:
import inspect,sys
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import bl_dispatch as b
s=inspect.getsource(b.self_eval_rules)
ok=('rag.py eval --root _self' not in s) or ('before your edits' in s) or ('pre-edit' in s)
print('brief names the landing eval or a pre-edit count',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Review 2026-10-18: `python3 _tools/rag.py eval --root _self | tail -1` gives noted=4, `python3 _tools/rag.py eval | tail -1` gives noted=13 = NOTED_BASELINE. The gate answer ST-sgzhsq4p g1 (a fixed rule in the brief) stays; the reviewer asked to change the command it names.
